name: Lead Intake → Score → CRM → Follow-ups (concept demo)

parameters.content:
## ⚙️ Setup checklist — do this after import

**1. Supabase** — create the tables, then replace `YOUR-PROJECT-REF` and `YOUR_SUPABASE_KEY` in the two Supabase nodes:
```sql
create table leads (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  name text, email text, service text, budget text,
  message text, score int, tier text,
  reasons jsonb, spam_flag boolean default false,
  received_at timestamptz default now()
);
create table call_tasks (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  lead_email text, lead_name text, score int,
  due_day int default 3, status text default 'open',
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
```
Use the **service_role** key if RLS blocks inserts, or add an open insert policy.

**2. Slack** — in Slack: Apps → Incoming Webhooks → add to #new-leads → paste the URL into the Slack node (replaces `hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/PATH`).

**3. SMTP** — open the two email nodes and attach your SMTP credential (Gmail App Password, Postmark, etc.). Also set `hello@YOUR-DOMAIN.com` as the sender.

**4.** Activate the workflow, then point the website form at the **Production URL** shown on the Webhook node.

**5.** Test with: `curl -X POST <webhook-url> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Test","email":"test@company.com","service":"website","budget":"500-2000","message":"Need a new site asap"}'`

## 1 — Webhook trigger

Receives the website form POST. n8n gives you a Test URL and a Production URL — use the Production URL in the form's `action` (or your fetch call) once the workflow is Active.

## 2 — Lead scoring (Code)

Transparent rule-based engine, 0–100:

- Budget: under $500 → +5 · $500–2k → +20 · $2–10k → +35 · $10k+ → +45
- Service: AI automation +20 · website/booking +15 · CRM +12 · fix +8
- Urgency keywords (asap/urgent/this week) → +10
- Timeline words (deadline/launch) → +5
- Business email domain → +10
- Spam patterns (SEO/crypto/rank guarantees) → −30 + flag

Tier: ≥75 HOT · 45–74 WARM · <45 COLD.

Edit the rules here AND in the web demo's `lib/scoring.ts` together.

## 3 — CRM insert (Supabase)

Saves the scored lead via the Supabase REST API. Replace:

- `YOUR-PROJECT-REF` → your project ref
- `YOUR_SUPABASE_KEY` → anon key (or service_role if RLS blocks)

Prefer the native Supabase node? Swap this HTTP node for it — same fields.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ name: $json.name, email: $json.email, service: $json.service, budget: $json.budget, message: $json.message, score: $json.score, tier: $json.tier, reasons: $json.reasons, spam_flag: $json.spamFlag, received_at: $json.receivedAt }) }}

parameters.content:
## 4 — Day 0: instant confirmation

Sent within a minute of the form submit. Attach your SMTP credential to this node and set the sender address. Keep it short and human.

parameters.subject: =Thanks {{ $json.name }} — we received your request
parameters.message:
=Hi {{ $json.name }},

Thanks for reaching out about {{ $json.service }} — we got your request and will reply within one business day.

If it's urgent, just reply to this email.

— The team

parameters.content:
## 5 — Wait 1 day

Pauses the execution, then continues with the Day-1 follow-up. Waits survive n8n restarts.

## 6 — Day 1: follow-up email

Second touch. Personalize per tier with an IF on `$json.tier` if you want hot leads to get a different message (or an SMS via Twilio).

parameters.subject: =Quick follow-up on your {{ $json.service }} request
parameters.message:
=Hi {{ $json.name }},

Just checking in on your {{ $json.service }} request from yesterday — happy to answer any questions or jump on a quick call.

What would be a good time?

— The team

parameters.content:
## 7 — Wait 2 more days

Then creates the Day-3 call task. Total cadence: Day 0 → Day 1 → Day 3.

## 8 — Day 3: call task

Drops an open call task into Supabase so the owner sees “call this lead” in their CRM/tasks view instead of relying on memory.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_email: $json.email, lead_name: $json.name, score: $json.score, due_day: 3, status: "open" }) }}

parameters.content:
## 9 — Hot-lead branch

Runs in parallel off the scoring node: if `score ≥ 75`, the owner gets a Slack alert within seconds. The main chain (CRM → emails) continues regardless — the IF's empty branch simply ends.

## 10 — Slack alert (hot leads only)

Posts to #new-leads via an Incoming Webhook — no OAuth needed. Create it in Slack (Apps → Incoming Webhooks) and paste the URL below, replacing the placeholder.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: ':fire: HOT LEAD — ' + $json.name + ' (' + $json.score + '/100)\n' + $json.email + ' · ' + $json.service + ' · budget ' + $json.budget + '\n"' + String($json.message).slice(0, 200) + '"' }) }}
